label: Fused MoE epilogue
mechanism: silu(gate)*up folds into the NVFP4 activation-quant kernel between the two grouped expert GEMMs, deleting 9 eager elementwise passes over the 128-row-padded expert row space in BOTH phases
hypothesis: The native-MMA W4A4 routed-expert path (exp-0015a/0015b, the accepted lineage) is the ONLY one of the engine's three grouped-expert GEMMs that does not fuse its inter-GEMM epilogue: kernels/moe_gemm.py:183 (W4A16) and kernels/moe_gemm_bf16.py:104 (layer 2) both compute (g*sigmoid(g))->bf16->fp32 * u inside their own GEMM epilogue, while the CUTLASS CuTe-DSL grouped kernel has no fusable epilogue, so exp-0015a fell back to an eager torch chain: gu=c1.view(m_cap,ffn,2); g=gu[...,0].float(); u=gu[...,1].float(); ((g*sigmoid(g)).to(bf16).float()*u).to(bf16).contiguous(), then a separate nvfp4_quant read of that activation. That chain is 9 elementwise passes plus the quant kernel's own read, and it runs over the PADDED row space m_cap, not over the real rows: the graphed decode step's m_cap is 32896 (B=64 x top6 = 384 real pair rows; the 128-row-per-expert tile padding is what exp-0015b's ledger row called the honest cost of the native MMA), and a canonical G=6 prefill cohort's is 59392. Counted in bytes that is ~6.7 GB/layer of HBM traffic in decode and ~11 GB/layer in prefill to produce values the quant kernel could compute in registers between the load it already makes and the store it already makes. ONE VARIABLE: kernels/fp4_quant.py's existing quant kernel gains a SILU constexpr branch (the source row is 2*ffn wide with interleaved gate/up columns - the checkpoint's w13 row interleave carried through the GEMM - so one contiguous 2*BLOCK_K load plus the tl.split the packer already uses gives gate and up in registers), the rounding chain copied verbatim from the two kernels that already fuse it, and moe_experts_w4a4 calls nvfp4_quant_silu(c1, ffn, gs2) instead of the chain + nvfp4_quant. Nothing else moves: same GEMMs, same shapes, same routing, same epilogue, same grid, no new allocation (the [m_cap, ffn] bf16 activation and its four fp32 temporaries are never allocated, so the captured graph pool SHRINKS by ~1.6 GB/device/segment). MEASURED, GPU 4, engine/pyengine/tests/t_fused_epilogue.py (log /workspace/logs/t_fused_epilogue_exp0022_out.log), at BOTH phases' real m_cap shapes: (arm a) EQUIVALENCE - the fused kernel is BITWISE equal to the eager chain: 0 of 50,528,256 packed bytes differ at the decode shape, 0 of 91,226,112 at the prefill shape, scales bitwise, dequantized max|delta| exactly 0.000e+00. This is not an envelope claim; the engine's arithmetic is unchanged bit for bit, which is why the D13 parity block must be identical to the accepted lineage's. (arm b) two identical runs bitwise equal - the t_b3-adapted same-schedule determinism arm. (arm c) SPEED, CUDA-event timed, interleaved arms after discarded warm-ups: decode m_cap=32896 1.529 -> 0.110 ms/layer (13.9x, -1.419 ms/layer); prefill m_cap=59392 2.724 -> 0.193 ms/layer (14.1x, -2.531 ms/layer). (arm d) CAPTURE SAFETY - captured in a CUDA graph and replayed, the fused kernel gives bitwise the same bytes as the eager launch, and a second replay is identical (the decode step is a captured region, exp-0012). REAL-WEIGHT A/B, the same test the accepted W4A4 rows were gated with, run twice in one session over the kill switch (engine/pyengine/tests/t_moe_w4a4.py on real layer-3 routed experts, E=256/K=6144/ffn=3072): arm f whole-layer moe_experts wall at T=736 goes 3.84 ms (PYENGINE_FUSED_EPILOGUE=0) -> 2.24 ms (fused) = 1.71x on the ROUTED-EXPERT LAYER ITSELF, while arms c (vs the independent fp32 emulation and the _scaled_mm arbiter), d (determinism) and e (W4A4-vs-W4A16 rel_mean 1.784e0 / cos 0.9888) print byte-identical reports in both arms - the change is invisible to every correctness arm and visible only in the wall. For scale: the W4A16 kernel this lineage replaced reads 10.91 ms on that same arm. BASE, stated plainly: e30e841 (exp-0021, ledger iter 22, REJECTED at 223.5 vs the 223.6 bar - it missed by 0.04%, i.e. it is thin, not harmful, and its deferred-readback plumbing is inherited unchanged with its PYENGINE_DECODE_FIRST=0 kill switch) merged with current main; git merge-base --is-ancestor main b1a28ba verified at spec time. The exp-0021 post-mortem is appended to experiments/DEADENDS.md in that merge, along with the cheap kill of this iteration's first hypothesis (CUTE DSL from_dlpack marshalling: measured 5.7-6.8 us/call, ~4 ms/traversal, not the fat).
predicted_delta: +30 to +55% timeboxed decode_heavy tok/s: 290-345 vs the best same-protocol accepted row 222.9 (merge bar 223.6). Cycle model, stated so it can be falsified - it is the same model that reproduced the accepted 221.8/222.9 rows within 2% (exp-0018/exp-0021): ~180 prefill traversals x 1.373 s = 247 s + ~2166 graphed decode steps x 0.168 s = 364 s = 611 s. The measured per-layer deltas apply to the 63 NVFP4 MoE layers (3-65; layer 2's bf16 twin already fuses, layers 0-1 are dense): decode 63 x 1.419 ms = -89 ms/step and prefill 63 x 2.531 ms = -159 ms/traversal, giving 180 x 1.214 + 2166 x 0.079 = 218 + 171 = 389 s of work in the same box -> 611/389 = 1.57x -> ~350. I discount that to 290-345 because the isolated arms cannot see in-situ effects (allocator reuse inside the captured pool, and whatever fraction of the 168 ms step is not the routed-expert path). FLOOR CASE, and it is what makes this worth running even if the model is optimistic: the saving is a fixed number of GPU-milliseconds per step on a step that exp-0012 established is GPU-bound with a locked dispatch floor, on kernels whose shapes are pinned by the graph, so the only way it lands below ~260 is if the in-situ epilogue share is materially smaller than two independent measurements (synthetic m_cap arm and real-weight layer A/B, which agree at -1.42 vs -1.60 ms/layer once scaled for m_cap) both say. A result near 223 would mean the graphed step is not spending the time those kernels demonstrably take, which would itself falsify the exp-0012 kernel table this whole ranking rests on. prefill_heavy rides the same seam with the larger per-layer delta and should gain more; remeasure later as a point row.
